uslaw-usc-t2-s142d:
Section 142d of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with a Library pay officer. The officer is the disbursing officer of the Library of Congress. He may pay out Library money only on vouchers in due form. The vouchers must be certified by the Librarian or a named stand-in.

The stand-in must be an officer or staff member cleared in writing. The pay officer must check each voucher as far as need be. The check is that the form is right and the marks are in place. He is held to account for the payments on that basis. A guard then frees him where a false paper misled the payment. In that case the fault rests on the one who certified it.
uslaw-usc-t2-s182d: Section 182d of Title 2 of the United States Code subjects certain Library of Congress funds to outside audit. The funds are the revolving funds created under sections 182a through 182d of the title. Each of those funds is subject to audit by the Comptroller General. The choice and timing of the audit rest at his discretion, not the library's. The whole rule is one sentence long.
uslaw-usc-t2-s282d: Section 282d of Title 2 of the United States Code covers official mail matter of the Office of Legislative Counsel. It sits in Chapter 9 of that title, on that office, in the House part, among its administrative rules. The rule is a single sentence. It states that the Legislative Counsel may send the official mail matter of the office as franked mail. That sending is made under section 3210 of Title 39 of the Code. The text is current through Public Law 119-134.
